LLM auditresponse for yogurt.js:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a small (109-line) Node preload/entry wrapper for the packaged Electron app, the kind of shim Arch Electron packages commonly install to make a binary-identical upstream build work when unpacked under `/usr/lib/<pkg>` instead of an Electron `resources/` directory.

Everything it does is local and path-scoped:
- `resolveAppDir()` inspects `process.argv` for `--app`/`--app=`, probes `/usr/lib/<name>/{app.asar,app,app.asar.unpacked}`, then falls back to `$_APPDIR` or `/usr/lib/@appname@` (the `@appname@` placeholder is substituted at package time).
- It redefines `process.resourcesPath` (non-writable) and, when a packaged app is detected, forces `ELECTRON_IS_DEV=0` / `NODE_ENV=production` so dev-only code paths aren't taken.
- It monkey-patches a set of **read-only** `fs` / `fs.promises` functions (`readFile`, `existsSync`, `statSync`, `readdirSync`, `createReadStream`, etc.) so paths under `<electron>/resources` are rewritten into the app dir. No write/delete/rename/permission APIs are touched.

The fs patching is the only unusual construct and it is a bounded string-prefix rewrite, not a generic interceptor: it requires `p` to start with `electronResources + path.sep`, rejects any relative path containing a `..` segment, and only rewrites when the first relative segment exists in the app dir's top-level listing (`topLevel.has(first)`). There is no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no base64/hex-decoded blob, no `child_process`, no `http`/`https`/`net` require, no `curl`/`wget`, no socket or reverse shell, no reading of `/etc/shadow`, SSH/GPG keys, browser data, or environment exfiltration, and no writes outside the app's own directory. The whole body is wrapped in try/catch that only logs a warning.

Notes (hygiene only, not threats): the script trusts the `_APPDIR`, `_APPDIR_NO_FS_REDIRECT`, and `_APPDIR_DEBUG` environment variables, so a process that can already set env vars for this binary could point it at another directory — but such a caller already controls the process and this grants no new capability. The global fs monkey-patch is also a mild maintainability/robustness concern (it affects all modules loaded afterwards in that process) and is disabled by `_APPDIR_NO_FS_REDIRECT`. Neither is evidence of injected malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Electron app-dir shim: local path fixes only, no network or obfuscation</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
For the narrow safety gate of running makepkg --printsrcinfo, the PKGBUILD is safe. The command executes the top-level scope of the PKGBUILD while sourcing it. The visible top-level content consists mainly of ordinary package metadata assignments, source and checksum arrays, and shell function definitions. Defining functions does not execute their bodies, and functions such as prepare, build, and package are not run by this command. No top-level download, eval, execution, exfiltration, or other operational code is present in the executed scope. Source URLs and checksums are inert during this step, and no fetching or verification occurs.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for yogurt.js:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a small Electron launcher shim (a wrapper script installed alongside the packaged app) that rewrites `process.resourcesPath` and redirects `fs` lookups from the stock Electron `resources` directory to the package's own application directory (e.g. `/usr/lib/@appname@`). It performs no network access, no `eval`/`Function`, no base64 or hex decoding, no child processes, and never writes or deletes anything on disk — it only computes paths and wraps read-only `fs` methods.

The most notable behavior is monkey-patching `fs`/`fs.promises` read functions so that paths under `path.dirname(process.execPath)/resources` are remapped into `appDir`. This is consistent with the package's stated purpose (making an unpacked Electron app find its `resources` relative to the Arch install location), and the redirect is defensive: it skips paths containing `..`, requires the first path component to exist in the app directory's top-level listing, and only applies to its own `resources` prefix. The environment variables consulted (`ELECTRON_IS_DEV`, `NODE_ENV`, `_APPDIR`, `_APPDIR_NO_FS_REDIRECT`, `_APPDIR_DEBUG`) are ordinary dev/packaging toggles, and the `--app` argv handling is standard Electron production-mode forcing.

No malicious indicators are present: nothing is fetched from an unexpected host, nothing is executed from decoded data, and no data outside the application's own scope is touched. At most one could note the fs interception as a design/transparency consideration, but it does not constitute a supply-chain attack.

</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Benign Electron launcher that remaps resourcesPath and fs reads into the app's own directory.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The two remote sources point to the project's declared upstream: the prebuilt `Yogurt-linux-x86_64.AppImage` from `github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/releases`, and the `LICENSE` from the same repository on `raw.githubusercontent.com`. Both are consistent with the package's stated purpose and homepage (`yogurt.so`). The remaining sources (`yogurt.js`, `yogurt.sh`) are local files shipped inside the AUR repo. All four entries have pinned `sha256sums` (none set to `SKIP`), which is good hygiene.

There are no suspicious network destinations, no obfuscation, no `eval`/base64/`curl|bash`, no VCS/mutable-ref sources, and no unexpected file or system operations. This is ordinary `-bin`-style packaging of a prebuilt Electron application. Nothing here deviates from standard practice in a malicious way.
</details>
